1893 Median and Quartiles using the CDF

examples.question_text: A continuous random variable has PDF $f(x)=\dfrac{3x^2}{117}$ on $[2,5]$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find its CDF, confirm $F(5)=1$, and calculate $P(X\le4)$ and $P(3\le X\le4)$.
examples.solution_text:
For $2\le x\le5$:
$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\int_2^x\frac{3t^2}{117}\,dt\\&=\left[\frac{t^3}{117}\right]_2^x\\&=\frac{x^3-8}{117}.\end{align*}$
The complete CDF is
$F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<2,\\\dfrac{x^3-8}{117},&2\le x\le5,\\1,&x>5.\end{cases}$
$F(5)=\dfrac{125-8}{117}=1$.
$\begin{align*}P(X\le4)&=F(4)\\&=\frac{64-8}{117}\\&=\frac{56}{117}.\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}P(3\le X\le4)&=F(4)-F(3)\\&=\frac{56}{117}-\frac{19}{117}\\&=\frac{37}{117}.\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A continuous random variable has PDF $f(x)=\dfrac{2e^{2x}}{e^8-1}$ on $[0,4]$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find its CDF and the exact probability $P(X>3)$.
A continuous random variable has PDF $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x\ln5}$ on $[1,5]$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find its CDF and the exact probability $P(2\le X\le4)$.
examples.solution_text:
For $1\le x\le5$:
$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\int_1^x\frac{1}{t\ln5}\,dt\\&=\frac1{\ln5}[\ln t]_1^x\\&=\frac{\ln x}{\ln5}.\end{align*}$
Thus
$F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<1,\\\dfrac{\ln x}{\ln5},&1\le x\le5,\\1,&x>5.\end{cases}$
$F(5)=1$.
$\begin{align*}P(2\le X\le4)&=F(4)-F(2)\\&=\frac{\ln4-\ln2}{\ln5}\\&=\frac{\ln2}{\ln5}.\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A continuous random variable has PDF $f(x)=\dfrac2{x^2}$ for $x\ge2$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find its CDF, describe its behaviour as $x\to\infty$, and calculate $P(3\le X\le6)$.

A continuous random variable has PDF
$f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac16,&0\le x<3,\\\dfrac14,&3\le x\le5,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$
Find its complete CDF, sketch it, and calculate $P(2<X<4)$.

A continuous random variable has PDF
$f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{3+x}{9},&-3\le x\le0,\\\dfrac{3-x}{9},&0<x\le3,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$
Find its complete CDF and sketch it.

A continuous random variable has CDF
$F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<0,\\\sin x,&0\le x\le\dfrac\pi2,\\1,&x>\dfrac\pi2.\end{cases}$
Find its PDF and verify that the total area is $1$.
examples.solution_text:
Differentiate the CDF on the interior of its support:
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=F'(x)\\&=\cos x,\qquad 0<x<\frac\pi2.\end{align*}$
A PDF is
$f(x)=\begin{cases}\cos x,&0\le x\le\dfrac\pi2,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$
Endpoint values do not affect probabilities. Since $\cos x\ge0$ on $[0,\frac\pi2]$, the density is non-negative.
$\begin{align*}\int_0^{\pi/2}f(x)\,dx&=\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos x\,dx\\&=[\sin x]_0^{\pi/2}\\&=1.\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A continuous random variable has CDF $F$, with $F(4)=0.3$ and $F(9)=0.8$. Find (a) $P(X\le4)$, (b) $P(4<X\le9)$, (c) $P(X>9)$, and (d) the probability that $X$ lies outside $[4,9]$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $P(X\le4)=F(4)=0.3$.
(b)
$\begin{align*}P(4<X\le9)&=F(9)-F(4)\\&=0.8-0.3\\&=0.5.\end{align*}$
(c)
$\begin{align*}P(X>9)&=1-F(9)\\&=1-0.8\\&=0.2.\end{align*}$
(d) The two tails are disjoint. Since $X$ is continuous, $P(X<4)=F(4)$.
$\begin{align*}P(X<4\text{ or }X>9)&=F(4)+1-F(9)\\&=0.3+0.2\\&=0.5.\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Integrating 3t²/117 from 2 to x gives (x³−8)/117. At 5 this equals 1. F(4)=56/117 and F(3)=19/117, so the interval probability is 37/117. Outside-support branches are correct.
The antiderivative of 2e^(2t)/(e⁸−1) is e^(2t)/(e⁸−1). Thus F(x)=(e^(2x)−1)/(e⁸−1), F(4)=1, and P(X>3)=(e⁸−e⁶)/(e⁸−1).
Integrating 1/(t ln 5) from 1 to x gives ln x/ln 5. The endpoint values are 0 and 1. F(4)−F(2)=ln(4/2)/ln 5=ln 2/ln 5.
Integrating 2t⁻² from 2 to x gives 1−2/x. F(2)=0 and its limit is 1. F(6)=2/3 and F(3)=1/3, giving interval probability 1/3.

The first piece accumulates x/6 and reaches 1/2 at 3. The second gives 1/2+(x−3)/4=(x−1)/4, reaching 1 at 5. F(4)−F(2)=3/4−1/3=5/12. The sketch joins (0,0), (3,1/2), and (5,1), with correct constant exterior branches.

The triangular density has total area (1/2)×6×(1/3)=1. Integration on the left gives (3+x)²/18 and F(0)=1/2. Carrying this forward on the right gives 1−(3−x)²/18. Both branches agree at 0 and reach the correct endpoints. The plotted expressions match these branches.

Differentiating sin x on the support interior gives cos x. This is non-negative on [0,π/2], and its integral is sin(π/2)−sin(0)=1. The zero exterior density and explanation of endpoint values are correct.

The cumulative probability is 0.3; the interval probability is 0.8−0.3=0.5; the upper tail is 1−0.8=0.2. The disjoint exterior tails sum to 0.3+0.2=0.5. Continuity justifies ignoring endpoint inclusion.
